work.title: Readela 0.3.0: release preparation — store images, store copy, release-facing documents and candidate packages
work.ownerAuthorization: Owner instruction of 2026-10-13, after the owner accepted the final popup and confirmed the build of c7c0244 in their own Chrome, and the release-preparation section of DEC-143 of the same day. It authorizes complete release preparation for 0.3.0 on the existing pull request: correcting release-facing documents that no longer describe the source; new store screenshots taken from the built extension on synthetic pages and a refreshed promotional tile where it is outdated; the final English store copy for both stores with the dashboard hand-off; the final build, the package and source-archive checks and their digests; focused commits and a plain push. It does not authorize a new feature or a change of what the extension does, requests, reads or stores; merging pull request 9 or marking it ready; a tag or a release; uploading or submitting a version to the Chrome Web Store or Firefox Add-ons; changing a live listing or privacy field; any use of publication credentials; or a write to Personal OS.

parentPreflight.reason: That record and the three popup records after it place store images and store copy out of scope, as the work of ENT-243. This is that work, separately bounded, so it carries its own assertion. Those records stay the records for the code they cover and are not edited.

inScope: This record, committed first on the existing branch from baseCommit.

README.md, docs/store-listing.md, docs/privacy-policy.md and docs/privacy-and-permissions.md, and docs/architecture.md and docs/product-brief.md only where a release-facing statement contradicts the source: corrected to describe the 0.3.0 source as it is. Dated evidence already recorded is not rewritten.
src/manifest/base.json: the description string only, which the Chrome Web Store shows as the summary. No other manifest entry.

scripts/store-images.mjs and the synthetic pages it serves, written for the listing: screenshots of the built extension, a contact sheet and reduced copies for checking legibility. docs/store-images/ regenerated from them.

The existing verification run against the result: the dev-standards verifier, the unit tests, the end-to-end suite in Chrome and Firefox, the packages, the source archive and their digests, and a check that the packages hold what the documents say and nothing else.
Dated evidence under docs/evidence/, candidate packages and generated evidence kept outside the repository under the project's evidence convention, and an accurate description of pull request 9.
outOfScope: Everything that runs in a page, the popup's markup, style and behaviour, the background component, the commands, permissions, match patterns, web-accessible resources, stored forms, the fonts, supported sites and browsers, and the version number.
A new feature, a new brand identity, optional marketing material beyond the listing's own images.
A repeat of the hour-long memory comparison, unless this work shows a regression that calls for it.
Dependency changes, a new build or packaging system.
Merging pull request 9, marking it ready, a v0.3.0 tag, a release, an upload or submission to either store, a change to a live listing, and any write to Personal OS.

risk.note: Nothing is published by this work. What it prepares is published later, and a published version can only be superseded: so every statement in the copy is checked against the source, every image is taken from the built extension, and the candidate archives are bound by SHA-256 to one commit. The archives the stores receive are built from the frozen commit after integration, under the Gates of that stage.

ordering: This assertion committed first; documents, the manifest string and the image script after it; then the build, the checks, the images and the candidate archives from that source; then dated evidence. Integration, the frozen commit, the final archives, a publication Gate per provider and the submissions are later stages with their own authorization.

invalidators: Work leaves the declared scope: a file that runs in a page, the popup, the background component or any manifest entry other than the description would have to change.
A permission, match pattern, web-accessible resource, stored form, command or the version number would have to change.
A statement about privacy or permissions can be made true only by changing the extension.
Declared Capabilities or Exceptions change, or the applicable baseline identity changes.
Project Operating Protocol semantics materially change before the work is closed.
